title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 136
paragraphs: But when day came, those left behind perceived that they had been betrayed by Darius, and they held out their hands in submission to the Scythians, explaining their situation. When the Scythians heard this, they joined together as quickly as possible—the two combined divisions of the Scythians, and the single division, along with the Sauromatai, Budinoi, and Gelonians—and began to pursue the Persians, heading straight for the Ister. But since the Persian army was mostly foot and was not familiar with the roads (the roads not being marked), while the Scythian army was made up of horsemen and knew the shortest cuts, they missed one another and the Scythians arrived at the bridge much before the Persians. Then, having learnt that the Persians had not yet arrived, they said to the Ionians who were in the ships: “Ionians, the days of your number are past, and you are not acting uprightly in continuing to wait. As you stayed before from fear, so now break up the passage as quickly as you can, and depart free and unhurt, feeling thankfulness both to the gods and to the Scythians; and as for the one who was formerly your master, we shall so convince him that he will never again march with an army against any nation.”
